21. what lüscher did: 
Include/exclude Uri — pp. 132–133, Figure 43	Compared the relationship between average district size and disproportionality before and after reform, both including and excluding Uri. Uri combines PR in districts with ≥5 seats with majority voting in smaller districts and had only one post-reform observation.	Excluding Uri made the pattern clearer: cantons with smaller districts experienced larger reductions in disproportionality. After reform, disproportionality was low and essentially unrelated to district size.
Exclude Graubünden — pp. 126 and 132	Excluded GR from the counterfactual analysis and the district-size assessment because relevant pre-reform data were missing under its former majoritarian system.	This was a data-driven exclusion, without an accompanying with/without comparison.
Account for different electoral thresholds — p. 125	Constructed an effective-threshold variable using different rules for conventional PR, biproportional elections, and statutory quorums. Where two quorums existed, he used the canton-wide quorum.	This accounts for implementation differences in the variable construction; he does not report sensitivity checks using alternative threshold definitions.
